about: ASL numbers 1-10 for the numbers practice app, rendered 24 Oct 2026 (research/numbers-2026-10-24/gloves). 1-9: the average hand of the FSboard signers (Google, 90 Deaf signers in the two downloaded landmark files, CC BY 4.0): phone-number clips cut into digits by forced alignment (align_digits.py), each segment's window-median hand kept only if the numbers grader accepts it as that number, every signer's hands averaged first, then each bone's direction averaged over signers (hand_pose_<n>.json), and the hand turned the way the signers held it to their camera (the chordal mean of their palm frames). In 1 and 2 the curled fingers are closed into a firm curl (MCP 88, PIP 100 deg, DIP as averaged) and in 1 the thumb is laid over the curled middle finger: averaged curled fingers came out as a loose claw that MediaPipe misread on the render (the grader rejected both). 10 (TEN, a thumbs-up; no FSboard data): the signers' average A, the fingers closed into a tight fist and the thumb straightened along the hand's long axis, upright with the palm turned 20 deg to the signer's left; the side-to-side twist is not shown. Posed on the V-ARM 05 rigged hand in Blender Cycles (render_gloves.py) with a smooth lavender glove material, soft studio light and the forearm cut 4 cm before the wrist, a straight-on camera, then mirrored so each is a RIGHT hand as it looks on the learner's own (mirrored) screen, cut out on transparency and saved 720 px on the long side (finish.py). W is the wrist and M the middle finger's knuckle (landmark 9), as fractions of the image (x from the left, y from the top): the posed rig's joints projected through the render camera. MediaPipe's reading of each glove on grey puts the knuckle within 0-4% of the long side of M and the wrist 2-6% (median 3%) nearer the knuckles than W; every 1-9 glove, read back by MediaPipe at three sizes, is accepted by the numbers grader (research/numbers-2026-10-24/model.json) as its own number (verification.json). Installed for the numbers build as assets/gloves/<n>.png (tools/build-numbers-site.sh); listed under `letters`, the key the app reads.
